title: Kitchen Cabinet Painting in Dunnellon, FL
description: Kitchen cabinet painting in Dunnellon, FL: doors, drawer fronts, boxes, and islands degreased, primed, and finished in urethane enamel with minimal downtime.
h1: Kitchen Cabinet Painting in Dunnellon, FL
heroIntro: New color on your kitchen cabinets, islands, and drawer fronts without ripping anything out. Here is exactly what happens to each part of the kitchen and how long you work around us.

sections.h2: What gets painted, piece by piece
body: Kitchen cabinet painting in Dunnellon, FL covers more parts than most people count. Here is how our Dunnellon crews break the job down. Each is handled a little differently:
bullets: Doors and drawer fronts: removed, labelled by location, and finished away from the boxes for a smooth sprayed surface
Cabinet boxes, face frames, and end panels: degreased, scuffed, primed, and finished in place
Islands: treated like their own piece, often in a contrasting color
Crown, light rail, and toe kicks: included so the trim matches the doors
Hardware: removed, bagged by location, and reinstalled at the end

body: Every kitchen has an invisible layer of cooking residue, heaviest on the doors flanking the range and the drawer fronts nearest the stove. Primer will stick to that residue, not to the wood, and the new finish ends up chipping along the edges within a year. So the first day of a kitchen job is cleaning: a cabinet-specific degreaser, a clean-water rinse, and a full scuff-sand that takes the old sheen down evenly. Only then does primer go on. It is slow, unglamorous work, and it is why a professional cabinet finish outlasts a weekend project.
Oak cabinets need one more step. Open grain shows through paint as fine lines unless it is filled. Our article on painting oak cabinets shows the difference.

Topcoats are waterborne urethane enamel, which levels smoothly, cures hard, and wipes clean. Two full coats are standard. In a Dunnellon kitchen where humidity runs high, we give each coat the conditions it needs to cure before the next goes on, rather than rushing to hit a date. Before spraying, we paint a large sample of the chosen color and hold it up against your countertop and backsplash, since stone and tile shift how a cabinet color reads.

sections.h2: Living with the kitchen during the work
body: This is the question every owner asks. The kitchen stays partly usable for most of the project. Counters, appliances, floors, and the backsplash are covered, and the fridge and sink stay accessible on most days. While doors are out, the boxes are open, so plan simple meals. The days when boxes are wet are marked on the schedule ahead of time. The full timeline is written into the estimate, not guessed at on the first morning.

Keeping your existing pulls? They go back on the same holes. Switching to a new style with different spacing? Tell us at the walkthrough so filling old holes and drilling new ones can be added to the scope. For vanities, built-ins, and laundry cabinets elsewhere in the house, see our broader cabinet refinishing page for Dunnellon. If you are still weighing a remodel, read refinish vs. replace, and see the main cabinet painting service for more on our process.

faqs.q: Can my island be a different color from the perimeter cabinets?
faqs.a: Yes. Two-tone kitchens are common, and the island is simply listed as its own line item with its own color.

faqs.q: Will I be able to use my kitchen?
faqs.a: For most of the project, yes, with some limits. The days when boxes are wet and off-limits are marked on the schedule in advance.

faqs.q: Do you paint the inside of the cabinets?
faqs.a: Interiors are optional and listed separately. Most owners paint the exterior faces and the door edges only.
